projects.title: More document requests
projects.feasibility_gate: Supported model/backend disaggregation and verified transfer path.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: tuned aggregated LLM serving versus Dynamo prefill/decode separation with equal total GPU count, model revision, weight/KV precision, and workload. Seed from the selected Llama or Qwen result only after resolving engine support and sufficient context.
projects.controls: prompt/output distributions, arrival process, service targets, GPU allocation, prefill/decode split, TP/replicas, chunked prefill, transfer connector, locality, routing, and cache state. Screen feasible splits within a fixed candidate budget. Do not assume every TP size or disaggregated path works on RTX PRO. Optional prefill-count and fixed arrival-rate grids with explicit TTFT and queue-growth targets; retain every failed cell. Optional joint goal search varies document and answer lengths and GPU splits, adaptively brackets demand, and exports separate capacity and latency peaks with every measured curve.
projects.implementation: Dynamo deployment adapter; transfer/topology preflight; request timestamps and queue/transfer metrics; AIPerf load curves and selected GuideLLM cross-checks. Launch services as an owned dependency graph and keep a matched engine configuration available for A.

outputs.title: completed-response latency reduction at matched load

projects.output_constraints: P01-O1 qualified requests/hour gain; P01-O2 completed-response latency reduction at matched load; P01-O3 GPU-scaling curve with explicit baseline. O3 needs additional GPU-count cells; O2 cannot be inferred from peak throughput alone.
projects.acceptance: measured A and B, same resource and quality contract, recorded KV transfer cost, client headroom checks, confirmed capacity boundary or clearly marked search limit. No assumed speedup from the NVIDIA B200/GB200 article.

projects.title: More document-analysis capacity
projects.feasibility_gate: Measure sustainable document populations, CPU reloads and queue pressure at fixed per-session activity.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: GPU-only prefix caching versus the same deployment with CPU KV offload. Normal automatic GPU cache sizing, identical sticky routing and question schedules. A separate resume diagnostic remains available.
projects.controls: Same model revision, precision, runtime, GPU count, context, document sizes and question cadence. Include cold starts and natural document replacement; preserve all load points and errors.
projects.implementation: Scheduled document-capacity replay with exact extraction scoring, NUMA-local replicas, bounded queues and CPU cache counters. Synthetic fixtures require representative validation before broad document-analysis claims.
projects.output_constraints: P02-O1 reusable conversation capacity; P02-O2 resume-latency reduction; P02-O3 avoided prefill/recomputation. Sustainable simultaneously active sessions are an additional independently measured curve, not a renaming of retained conversations.
projects.acceptance: timed return traces, full/cold misses retained, p95 resume gate, quality consistency, cache namespacing, and explicit tier occupancy. Disk and GPU capacities are not blindly summed when tiers duplicate blocks.

projects.title: More context per GPU
projects.feasibility_gate: Verified GPU/model/backend/cache-format path and long-context quality set.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: the existing FP8 cache configuration versus supported calibrated/lower-bit cache or compression candidates; BF16 supplies a quality reference. Keep model weights and supported context limit fixed.
projects.controls: cache format, calibration artifact, attention backend, prompt and output headroom, context ladder, concurrency, GPU memory budget, and corpus/quality thresholds. Candidate formats are enabled only after a kernel smoke test and allocation verification.
projects.implementation: cache capability matrix keyed by GPU architecture, engine, kernel, model, and dtype; calibration preparation; context-boundary search; long-context correctness tests; memory traces. Raising the experiment request limit must not silently raise a model's context limit or the old BenchmarkSpec limit.

outputs.title: concurrent-session gain at a fixed length

projects.output_constraints: P03-O1 maximum qualified input-length gain; P03-O2 concurrent-session gain at a fixed length; P03-O3 KV-memory reduction and quality tradeoff. O2 requires a separate concurrency sweep; theoretical bytes/token savings do not prove it.
projects.acceptance: no silent fallback dtype or truncation, fresh quality corpus, metadata/scales included in memory totals, and no context-extension claim beyond the validated model limit. Mark experimental kernel paths explicitly.

projects.title: Faster completed answers
projects.feasibility_gate: Compatible draft or speculative method; target-model and task-quality checks.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: target model normal decoding versus the same target with a compatible speculative method. Include draft compute and memory in the resource budget. Do not compare against a smaller independent answering model.
projects.controls: draft revision/method, draft-token count, target sampling settings, output policy, offered load, and concurrency. Begin with deterministic structured tasks, tested code/SQL generation, or evidence-grounded summaries rather than arbitrary fixed tokens alone.
projects.implementation: draft asset lifecycle, supported model/draft pairing, effective speculative config capture, acceptance/verification counters, workload graders, and AIPerf/GuideLLM serving measurements where their request protocol fits.

outputs.title: energy per correct answer if wall telemetry is present

projects.output_constraints: P04-O1 completed-answer latency reduction; P04-O2 qualified task-throughput increase; P04-O3 energy per correct answer if wall telemetry is present. Acceptance rate is diagnostic evidence, not the headline.
projects.acceptance: draft and target fingerprinted, output/quality validation, fixed-load latency comparison and independent capacity curve, low- and high-load coverage. A method losing at high load remains in the report; no general speedup from a single best cell.

projects.title: More usable images
projects.feasibility_gate: Compatible teacher/student or budgeted distillation; blind acceptance rubric.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: tuned multi-step teacher diffusion versus a corresponding compatible student through FastGen. Prefer a verified existing student for the first implementation; support explicit distillation jobs when no suitable checkpoint exists.
projects.controls: teacher/student revisions, method, steps, precision, image dimensions, batch/concurrency, prompts, seeds, guidance, negative prompts, generation timeout, retries, and acceptance rubric. A teacher step-count sweep prevents an inflated comparison against an unnecessarily slow baseline.
projects.implementation: isolated FastGen environment/container; checkpoint download or resumable training job; teacher/student inference adapter; image artifact storage and hash index; blind review UI and structured rubric import/export. Validate automatic scoring against a human-reviewed subset. Never substitute FID or a single aesthetic score for task acceptance without justification.

outputs.title: cost per accepted image and distillation break-even

projects.output_constraints: P05-O1 accepted images/hour gain; P05-O2 generation-time reduction per accepted image; P05-O3 wall-energy reduction per accepted image; P05-O4 cost per accepted image and distillation break-even. Training cost is separate from inference; break-even exists only if the measured per-image savings are positive.
projects.acceptance: compatible model/method, same output dimensions and prompt mix, preserved rejected samples and regeneration costs, pending-review state, and measured quality uncertainty. Training success alone does not make a usable student or a positive claim.

projects.title: More business workflows per GPU
projects.feasibility_gate: Supported partition profiles or explicit software sharing; tested rollback.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: Whisper transcription plus a selected language model for structured post-call summaries: two dedicated GPUs versus one software-shared GPU and one GPU with two MIG partitions. The earlier independent-endpoint workflow remains available.
projects.controls: Identical audio, ASR model and precision, language model and precision, fixed call arrivals, summary grading, KV budget, stage timing and owned MIG restoration. Handoff is host-mediated text; no assumed PCIe bypass.
projects.implementation: partition discovery and plan; physical GPU/MIG UUID mapping; transactional create/restore with host lease; service packing; multi-endpoint traffic; per-tenant goodput and interference metrics. Only show partitions and guest/container paths supported by the exact stack.

outputs.title: resource or cost reduction for a fixed service set

projects.output_constraints: P06-O1 qualified-service density increase; P06-O2 reduction in tenant interference; P06-O3 resource or cost reduction for a fixed service set. Fixed-set cost needs equal demand and accounting, not merely the maximum-density result.
projects.acceptance: every counted service meets its contract concurrently; failed/starved tenants remain in totals; original GPU configuration restored; no confidential-computing claim implied by MIG isolation.

projects.title: Confidential inference
projects.feasibility_gate: Verified platform/guest/GPU protection combination and attestation; optional SGX/MIG independently gated.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: conventional VM versus an attested confidential VM with identical assigned resources. Bare metal is an additional diagnostic arm, not a substitute for the VM baseline. Add optional SGX key/policy service and supported device protection as separately declared components.
projects.controls: TDX/platform firmware, guest image digest, protected transfer mechanism, GPU CC mode, attestation policy, key-release configuration, service resource budget, and optional partitioning only if explicitly supported. Distinguish Intel TDX Connect, NVIDIA Protected PCIe, and encrypted bounce-buffer transfer; no interchangeable labels.
projects.implementation: read-only support/firmware preflight; VM/deployment adapter; attestation verifier and policy probes; secret-reference integration; capture of public evidence and measured protection state. Test refusal of invalid attestation and unauthorized key release using controlled fixtures. SGX needs a concrete application purpose and separate evidence. Provisioning/reboot is an explicit resumable setup operation with recorded host changes, not a hidden benchmark repair.

outputs.title: confidential tenant density only if the combined implementation is supported and measured

projects.output_constraints: P07-O1 protected capacity retained and overhead; P07-O2 security-control evidence report; P07-O3 confidential tenant density only if the combined implementation is supported and measured. O2 contains pass/fail scope and a threat model, not “X% more secure.”
projects.acceptance: validate the exact XE7740 stack rather than infer support from CPU branding. Do not automatically combine MIG with confidential GPU mode. No raw keys, credentials, or sensitive prompts in exports; offloaded KV requires its own protected-memory/storage boundary. Failed attestation blocks protected-performance claims. This is not certification or proof against all attacks.

projects.title: Lower energy consumption
projects.deprioritized_reason: Deprioritized 2026-10-25. Measured on XE7740: an idle GPU holding any CUDA context stays in P0 at about 86 W; locking clocks while the context is held parks it at about 32 W and unparks in 0.26 s. Standard autoscaling already releases idle GPUs to about 30 W, so parking adds almost nothing. Pack routing on top of autoscaling saves about 15-30% of GPU-board power in a model built from roofline sweeps (less at the wall). The savings are modest and only count where the customer pays per kWh, not per provisioned kW.
projects.feasibility_gate: Verified wall-power boundary and supported reversible power controls.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: normal power configuration versus supported power-limit/active-GPU/CPU-policy candidates. Compare the same accepted workload and completion deadline. Separate each control in screening before measuring a combined treatment.
projects.controls: supported power limits, active GPU count, CPU policy, warm/cold treatment, idle baseline, measurement duration, and quality/SLO requirements. Read supported ranges rather than hard-code wattages.
projects.implementation: wall sensor adapter for an available PDU or documented server PSU telemetry; timestamp alignment and integration; sensor coverage validation; reversible power changes; thermal/throttle records. Reuse request and quality evidence only if sensor windows cover those exact runs.

outputs.title: capacity gain at a fixed wall-power budget

projects.output_constraints: P08-O1 wall-energy reduction for fixed work; P08-O2 capacity gain at a fixed wall-power budget; P08-O3 measured energy/performance frontier. O2 requires a power-constrained load search; it cannot be computed by scaling O1.
projects.acceptance: wall boundary and uncertainty known, missing samples handled explicitly, no use of GPU package/RAPL counters as wall power, and restored original limits after failure or cancellation. Report gross and idle-adjusted energy separately if both are supplied.

projects.title: Lower cost per task
projects.feasibility_gate: Versioned prices, resource accounting, equal demand and quality.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: fixed reservations against dynamic allocation or another declared optimized deployment under an identical recorded demand trace. CPU/NUMA changes and model/precision substitutions are named treatment differences, with quality qualification for substitutions.
projects.controls: acquisition and support prices, amortization period, electricity, cooling assumption, software, operations, utilization, capacity reserve, demand trace, model-quality margin, and training/setup costs. Start with on-premises scenario comparison; cloud economics are optional dated inputs rather than implied measured cloud performance.
projects.implementation: timestamped price/assumption ledger, allocation-time accounting, whole-host versus marginal cost modes, demand replay, and versioned deterministic calculator. An analysis-only output may consume eligible existing campaigns; a dynamic-allocation performance claim needs an actual trace replay.

outputs.title: resources required for a fixed service demand

projects.output_constraints: P09-O1 cost reduction per accepted task; P09-O2 utilization/break-even sensitivity; P09-O3 resources required for a fixed service demand. Arithmetic freeing GPUs does not save capital unless the scenario actually avoids, removes, or productively reallocates that expense.
projects.acceptance: A and B cover equal demand/quality/availability assumptions, no double counting of shared hardware or allocated energy, idle costs retained, and measured inputs distinguished from prices and scenario assumptions. Updating prices creates a new analysis version, not a new measurement.

projects.title: Faster long-document responses
projects.feasibility_gate: Profiled bottleneck and compatible optimized kernel; unprofiled end-to-end confirmation.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: current supported attention implementation versus a compatible optimized attention/softmax path. Hold everything else fixed. Kernel-level softmax, attention fusion, and Dynamo routing softmax are different mechanisms; routing belongs under P02.
projects.controls: backend/kernel build, dtype, shapes, context length, concurrency, model revision, and numerical tolerance. First profile representative runs. Stop with a useful “no demonstrated opportunity” result if the bottleneck or compatible treatment is absent.
projects.implementation: profiler adapter and trace inventory; minimal operator check; numerical/quality validation; controlled backend selection; end-to-end confirmation with profiling disabled. Capture fallbacks and architecture requirements.
projects.output_constraints: P10-O1 end-to-end latency reduction; P10-O2 qualified throughput improvement; P10-O3 bottleneck/profile technical note. A kernel microbenchmark alone only qualifies O3.
projects.acceptance: supported RTX PRO execution path, no silent fallback, equivalent workload quality, numerical checks appropriate to precision, and end-to-end evidence. The linked Dynamo 0.4 article establishes a disaggregation direction, not a softmax-kernel result.

projects.title: All-US model and software stack
projects.feasibility_gate: Each candidate model loads and serves on the SM120 RTX PRO path under a US-stewarded engine with no silent fallback, using only pinned, offline-installable containers.
projects.baseline_and_treatment: US-only showcase, not a comparison with non-US models. Per tier (frontier, mid, small), every US-origin candidate runs on the same XE7740, workload, and service target, each at its own best supported engine and parallelism. The winner of each tier is the measured headline. Frontier candidates: Reflection Beam 1.0 501B-A23B NVFP4 (about 255 GB; tp4 x2 replicas versus tp8), with its DFlash2 drafter on and off; NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B NVFP4 (about 330 GB, tp8); Arcee Trinity Large if a fitting build exists. Mid: Nemotron 3 Super and gpt-oss-120b. Small: Gemma 4 26B and gpt-oss-20b.
projects.controls: model revision and checkpoint digest, precision, engine and container digest (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Dynamo; LMCache for any KV tier), TP/replicas, speculative decoding, context length, prompt/output distributions, arrival process, and service targets. Excluded components: KTransformers and Mooncake, along with any trust_remote_code loader code not pinned and reviewed. Reuse the open-loop roofline harness and the existing quality adapter with identical prompts for every candidate.
projects.implementation: per-model preflight (load, short serve, numerical sanity) before any campaign; open-loop capacity curves per candidate configuration; quality suite (coding, long-context recall, tool use); provenance capture of model license and origin, container digests, and an SBOM for every image; offline install from a local mirror through the ssh deploy branch path with outbound network blocked.

outputs.title: US-only capacity per XE7740 at SLO, frontier tier
best US model per tier: capacity and quality table
provenance and air-gapped deployment evidence report

projects.output_constraints: P11-O1 US-only capacity per XE7740 at SLO, frontier tier; P11-O2 best US model per tier: capacity and quality table; P11-O3 provenance and air-gapped deployment evidence report. O3 contains pass/fail scope and a threat model, not “X% more secure.” No claims about non-US models.
projects.acceptance: every reported model is US-origin, every serving component is US-stewarded and pinned, the deploy completes offline, quality passes the shared suite at the reported context, and capacity comes from the measured open-loop curves. A model that fails preflight is reported as unsupported on this platform, not dropped silently. Open-source projects have contributors from around the world; “US-stewarded” means US governance plus pinned, auditable code.
